By the matrix $H$ in Given and the circuit semantics [F7], applying $H$ to the first qubit sends the initial vector to $u=(|00\rangle+|10\rangle)/\sqrt2$. The basis in [F8] is orthonormal, so $\|u\|=1$; [F5]–[F6] therefore give the input density $\rho=|u\rangle\langle u|$.

The matrix of $\rho$ in [F8] has diagonal $(1/2,0,1/2,0)$ and nonzero off-diagonal entries only in positions $(00,10)$ and $(10,00)$, each $1/2$. Multiplication by the diagonal projectors gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_0)=1/2$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_1)=1/2$; the outcomes have these probabilities by [F3].

By [F4], the normalized conditional states are $P_0\rho P_0/(1/2)=|00\rangle\langle00|$ and $P_1\rho P_1/(1/2)=|10\rangle\langle10|$. On the outcome-$0$ branch the target is unchanged; on the outcome-$1$ branch the matrix $X$ in Given sends $|10\rangle$ to $|11\rangle$. The measured-and-controlled circuit therefore has the joint law stated.

The explicitly granted block matrix in Given sends $|00\rangle$ to $|00\rangle$ and $|10\rangle$ to $|11\rangle$. It therefore sends the premeasurement vector $u$ from step 1.2 to $u'=(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)/\sqrt2$. The ordered basis in [F8] makes $u'$ a unit vector, so [F5]–[F6] give the density operator $|u'\rangle\langle u'|$. Applying the diagonal projectors gives terminal weights $1/2$ on $00,11$ and zero on $01,10$ by [F3]. Thus the coherent circuit has the same joint law.

The displayed branches are the one-instrument, one-bit case of the coherent equivalence in [thm-qc-deferred-measurement]. The measurement label stays the first wire and the target update depends on that label.
